Do you read this in point 4 of the order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me, but that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Please read yourself then -- I might have some erroneous translation. Read point 4 of the order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not in the past tense, but in the future tense. That is the only error in your interpretation or translation. Upon the completion of its task, the commission "shall" compile a report in which it will show the following. The persons to be criminally prosecuted -- that means in the future, including all the evidence. Further on, "Individuals who are not to be criminally prosecuted" -- that also means in the future. "The wounded and sick persons" -- I guess that means among the questioned persons -- "and prisoners with incurable wounds or diseases." I have to say here that the commission was charged with something that, according to the law, it could not have been charged with. This commission could not decide on who of the questioned persons would be criminally prosecuted in the future, because it was up to the prosecutor's office, and that is a military court's prosecutor's office to make such a determination.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right, but do you agree with me that the Serbo-Croatian sentence means that the order asks the commission to find out which prisoners were suitable for proceedings; is that correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think what counsel is suggesting --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: -- is paragraph 4 is what the commission is directed to report on. This is what counsel is suggesting. You are expected to report on all these things indicated in paragraph 4. Is he correct to assume that that is what your report should contain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: If this was stated in the order in point 4, that means that you were expected to seek information in order to answer to these questions; is that not correct -- at least, that was the intention of the person who wrote the order of appointment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: My question is: no matter whether the report was given or not, do you remember having reached some information like that suitable to answer these four questions? I mean, not only as far as the suitability for proceedings is concerned but, also, to the other points -- did you reach some information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you are correct, we did reach such information. We were able to answer all four questions contained in paragraph 4, based on the statements taken from these individuals, and on this basis we could suggest which person would be suitable, as you put it, for criminal prosecution. For instance, persons who were in possession of weapons; also, persons who were not liable that way, and were also able to determine about those who were wounded and sick and who had incurable diseases and injuries because we had Dr Nadra Buturovic who was a member of the staff of the war hospital in Konjic and whose job within this commission was precisely to answer questions relating to these last two items in paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So, when you say "we could suggest which persons", et cetera, et cetera, with which document did you suggest that? Do you recall something more about the possibility of having given a report, or otherwise in which document or with which act did you give this answer about these points?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean the evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: No, I mean you said that you reached the answer on these questions and you reported -- you suggested -- you answered? When you say you "answered", to whom did you say you answered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, I said that we were in a position to answer these questions. It is possible that our answers were contained in this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually he does not really now remember. We might adjourn at this point until 2.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Kindly remind the witness that he is still on his oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I remind you, Sir, that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, Mr. Begtasovic. I think you still have in front of you Defence Exhibit D7/1, do you, otherwise I would request -- yes, the appointment order of 5 January 1993. So, in point 1 of this order, one can see that Jasminka Dzumhur was appointed president of the Commission. Did you know already Jasminka Dzumhur already when you were appointed as a member of the 4th Corps Commission -- did you know her already?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: What did she do before working with you in this 4th Corps Commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: You do not know. Before starting the work of your Commission, did all members have a meeting among you before starting -- did you discuss before starting the way you should proceed? How did you decide to proceed -- can you describe in some detail the method and procedure which you decided to apply before starting? Did you reach an agreement about the way of proceeding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With this time distance, I do not quite recall the time directly prior to the beginning of the work of the Commission, but, at any event, I think that a meeting of the kind you have described was held, because we had to reach an agreement on the method and way in which the order would be executed. At the meeting I probably took it upon myself to question the individuals and Dr Nadira Buturovic probably took it upon herself to examine the suspects from the medical standpoint. I think that Ms. Jasminka Dzumhur, as president of the Commission, coordinated our work and that Mr. Habdulah and Mr. Begic took part in the work of the Commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Does that mean, coming back to point 4 of the appointment order, that you decided also a method -- which method to follow in order to seek information about the wounded and sick among the prisoners you had to deal with; is that correct? You said about this lady, the doctor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the affirmative answer to your question can be given. But let me say once again that I do not remember exactly what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Do you not remember whether this lady -- I beg your pardon -- could you repeat the name of this lady doctor to me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dr Nadira Buturovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Dr Nadira Buturovic, do you remember whether she did perform medical examinations on the prisoners you had to deal with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, she did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you always, concerning this point 4 about wounded and sick -- did you decide also to ask the prisoners questions about possible wounds and health problems they might have to complain about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember asking questions of this kind, but at all events, questions of this kind I would have asked had I noticed, in the course of my talks, my questioning with these individuals, that they had been wounded or that they were ill. But I do not remember that I questioned anybody who was wounded or sick at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: At this time, Exhibit D7/1 can be given back to the Registrar. In your examination-in-chief, you said something about another similar investigating commission, which had to deal with prisoners a number of months before your Commission. Are you aware that this other commission was appointed around the second half of May -- it was active in Celebici mostly during the month of June 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say exactly whether it was the second half of May, but I do know that it was in one of the summer months.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you. You also mentioned some of its members -- you mentioned Goran Lokas, Miroslav Stenek and Mladen Zovko. Did you know them personally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember that detail precisely because I did know these individuals personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So, can you tell us which position did they have in Konjic -- these three persons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lokas, I cooperated with him for several years -- he was for several years at the head of the Konjic police. Mr. Stenek was a criminal inspector working for the Konjic police and Mr. Zovko, immediately before the war I seem to recall he worked in the police as well but at the centre for the security for Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Do you know that Goran Lokas had to withdraw immediately from the Commission because of a car accident he suffered at the end of May and that he did not return to the Commission any more?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that he had a car accident. He broke an arm and he did not return to the Commission after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Being a judge in Konjic and since you said that you spent your entire life in Konjic, we can expect that you know at least by name many persons who had some public responsibility in the municipality, so I am going to mention to you some other names, and I would like you to tell me if any of these people were also a member of the summer 1992 commission, as far as you know. So, Mirsad Subasic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he was there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Munib Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was there, too.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he was there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Sacir Pajic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Nusret Secibovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think he was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mehmedalija Rizvic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember that name and surname.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So, I take it that you do not know personally Sacir Pajic and Mehmedalija Rizvic, do you know them personally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, your Honour. There is a person in the public gallery who earlier was a witness for the Prosecutor. If she is not going to be a witness again, I do not care if she stays, but it is Sabina Manke, one of the investigators. If she is going to be a witness in the future, I would ask she leaves the public gallery.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: The Prosecution case is closed. We have no plans to call her.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That is fine. They have rebuttal. I did not want to be bringing this up at some later date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You have the answer and they are not likely to call such a witness again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That is correct. In that case, I have no objection to her staying. She is more than welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You do not intend to call her as your witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: No, there is one investigator for the OTP I may call, but she is not that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So, you remember four names among the ones I told you, and was any of them a colleague of you, a judge as you, either in Konjic or in any other court. I repeat the names, Mirsad Subasic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Munib Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was the deputy public prosecutor in Konjic, but he did not work in the court.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So, he was a kind of a -- in Yugoslavia judges and prosecutors consider themselves as colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You mean their appointments are interchangeable?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: They might shift one position from the another.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: In some countries the positions are interchangeable.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Is that correct, that in the former Yugoslavia, you could move from the position of judge to the one of prosecutor and vice versa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, you are right. The same conditions are necessary for appointment of judges and prosecutors.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: That is correct, thank you. So, let us say that Munib Halilovic somehow was a colleague of yours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know him, and he is not -- did not work in the justice organs of Konjic, definitely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: You do not know what was his position -- his official position, wherever he was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And Nasret Secibovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I remember, he worked in the public security station of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I forgot to say whether you know which was the position of Mirsad Subasic -- do you know him personally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know from hearing that he worked in the security station of Konjic. Perhaps I contacted with him at some point, but I cannot recall his face -- I do not know what he looks like. I cannot recall that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So, among these names I mentioned to you, who was the most familiar to you, or who were the most familiar to you -- maybe Munib Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. The most familiar were Goran Lokas, Miroslav Stenek, and Zovko Mladen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So, Mr. Begtasovic, did your Commission keep in consideration the investigations already done by the previous commission, and, if so, in this way, did you have their file? I think you said you had something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Yes, he said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: The file of the previous commission.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The witness did say precisely that he had a dossier, a file, with some statements and some files on their release.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right, it was my fault. I did not remember quite precisely. Who gave this file to you, Mr. Begtasovic, do you remember who gave this file to the 4th Corps Commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember -- after six years, I really cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: That is a fair statement, anyway. I would now like to show you two documents, which have to do with the previous commission and which are attached -- were attached by the Defence military expert witness, Brigadier Vejzagic, to his expert report. First, may I ask that the witness be provided with annex V-D/19 of Defence Exhibit D145/1, which is the third Vejzagic binder, please -- annex V-D/19. If you see this document, you see it is a document dated 18 June 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And it is entitled, "Summary of the Findings Regarding the Way of Arming the Serb Population"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you remember having seen and taking into consideration this document during the work of your Commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember that I have ever seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right. So, this document might be given back to the Registry. Now may I ask that the witness be provided with annex IV/9 of Defence Exhibit D144/1, which is the second Vejzagic binder, please. (Handed) As you see, it is a document dated 15 December 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And it is entitled, "Excerpts from Statements"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Can you please read out the stamp -- the heading, which appears right on top of the first page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "The Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina in situ for Investigating Crimes against Humanity and International Law at Sarajevo".

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: If you want to give a quick glance at the document to see how it appears to you, as I told you this is one of the documents which the military expert witness of the Defence relied upon for his expert report. Did you remember having seen and taken into consideration this document -- excerpts from statements -- in your work at the 4th Corps Commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember ever having seen this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Do you agree that this document appears to contain 136 excerpts from statements taken before December 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Really I do not understand the question. It contains excerpts -- why do you say "agree"?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Is that correct, that this document appears to contain 136 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He has never seen this document before, according to him. He does not remember seeing it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: He can look at it now. He is examining it and we are just describing it. Does that contain 136 paragraphs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me have a look first.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Yes, sure -- take your time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I notice that these are excerpts of statements of 136 individuals. The last number that I have come across seems to be 136.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: That is right. Would you please go to the excerpt number 122 in this document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: It contains a very short summary -- alleged -- of the information given by Veseljko Dzordzic , is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dzordzic Veseljko, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Would you please read it out -- there are four lines -- could you plead read it out?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness did not see this document before. Why should he read its contents out?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Because I have a question for him in my cross-examination, which requires him to read before these few lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: How he is associated with this document itself? Is he in any way connected with it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: He said he did not see this document, but I think the Prosecution can show this document to him and organise a specific question after that he had read a specific part of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: No, except you are trying to show that he has anything to do with it, or that he is concerned with it at all. He has no business with it. He has even told you he has never seen it before, he is seeing it for the first time and you now proceed to tell him to read out things, which somebody else might have made.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Your Honour, it does concern some work he was doing in any case -- this is why --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: These particular excerpts were part of the work he was doing?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Yes, because they are excerpts of statements --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Let us have the background to that, how he was in any way concerned with any preliminary work leading to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Do you see the 13 statements which were tendered on Friday by Ms. Residovic belonging to 13 persons who are included in this document, are they not? You can see, for instance, Kuljanin Radovan, Kuljanin Bosko, Dusko Bendzo, Mrsic Radovan, Kuljanin Marko -- all these prisoners who were interrogated by you and who are concerned by the 13 statements tendered Friday by Ms. Residovic, are all included in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: According to him, he merely recorded the statements of those persons. Even if those statements are in conflict with this small version, how can he explain that? That is for them to explain. He says he merely recorded their statements. Even if there is conflict, how would you impeach in reference to those statements?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I will move on to another issue. Did you consider any possible finding of the summer of 1992 commission about prisoners complaining of wounds and mistreatment, if you found any, in order to seek information about the wounded and sick according to point 4 of the order which appointed your Commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did not take into consideration these records of statements which we found in the files at all. I did say that I saw the statements of these individuals before our Commission was established, but we did not take them into account.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So you did not take into account the statements given by the same prisoners to the previous commission; is that what you say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: But did you happen to comment in your work in the 4th Corps Commission with any of the other members of the previous commission, Mladen Zovko, and Stenek, the ones you knew better?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I read in the report of Defence military expert Vejzagic on page 48 that your Commission's work turned out to be very short, because the legally determined judicial organs resumed their competencies. Is that a fair statement -- do you agree with this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that I could not link this to the resumption of work of the legally appointed authorities, as you put it, and I know that the district military court started work in the fall and I am not sure when the district military prosecutor's office began its work, and it would have been up to them initiate any criminal investigation and proceedings in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So you mean that this statement is not correct, as far as the reason for which your Commission work turned out to be very short, or do you mean that it is not correct because your Commission's work did not turn out to be very short.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually, that is an opinion of assessing the work --

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I would like him to elaborate on this basis and just tell us how long did the Commission actually work -- how long did the 4th Corps Commission --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: That is a fairer question than an opinion which someone else had of their work.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, your Honour. So, how long did the commission actually work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that they did not work more than one month.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So, your appointment being dated 5 January, can you say, when did you start interviewing the prisoners? Let me give you some assistance in order to put you in a condition to better remember. Looking at the 13 statements shown to you last Friday by Ms. Residovic, we can see that the earliest date is 9 January, which is in Exhibit 147/1. So, since you were appointed on 5 January, could 9 January be the first day when you started interviewing prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With your assistance, I think I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And, again, among those 13 statements, the latest date appearing on them is 18 January (Exhibits 153 and 154). Does that help you in recalling what might have been approximately the day when you completed the interviews?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Believe me, I do not remember, but I know that it did not last longer than one month. It could have lasted 15 days, and taking into account that we had 105 individuals, and that it would not have been possible to interrogate more than, say, 15 witnesses --

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Per day, you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, per day. In cases where we had rather short questioning, there would be up to 15 persons, let us say, if we took a 10-hour working day --

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If we took a 10-hour working day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I see. In that period of time, when you worked, how many working days did you actually employ in all, approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whatever I tell you now would be inaccurate. I can just guess or surmise. I could not really give you an exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So, in any case, you said you had to interview 105 prisoners; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that was the number, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Do you have a list of these prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me, I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I wonder if you have a list of these witnesses with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And they were all detained at Musala at that time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: May I ask again that the witness be provided with annex VII/4 of the third binder of expert witness Vejzagic. (Handed) You see this is a list of amnesties concerning 97 people. Do these 97 prisoners -- are these 97 persons part of the 105 prisoners you interviewed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The names of the persons whom I questioned, I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I see. But, in any case, you have been talking about the amnesty -- can you say, when was this amnesty granted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The law on amnesty was adopted, as far as I can recall, in 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Begtasovic, you stated that your Investigating Commission, in January 1993, conducted the proceedings, including the questioning of the prisoners according to the letter of the law, namely, according to the code of criminal procedure of Yugoslavia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. According to the laws of Yugoslavia, which was later adopted as the law in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Prior to the war, the law provided that persons could only be detained for three days without being brought to court, to a judge, or having formal proceedings initiated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And, before the war, if a person was kept for more than three days without having formal proceedings brought, without seeing a judge, that would be illegal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the war, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: But, would you agree that this continued to be the law, even after the war started?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So, would you agree that the fact that these persons were detained for a long time without having proceedings and seeing a judge was not according to the code of criminal procedure of Yugoslavia, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would disagree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Can you elaborate and tell me why?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will try. At that time, the basic court in Konjic did not work and neither did the higher court in Mostar, nor did the district military court, nor the competent prosecutor's offices and all these bodies that were involved in bringing charges and conducting criminal proceedings basically did not exist. Konjic was simply surrounded. There were no communications with the district court in Mostar, with the high court in Sarajevo, nor was there any communication with the district Prosecutor's Offices in Mostar or Sarajevo. This is why I say that the situation was different before the war from the one at the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Was there any law that said that persons could be detained indefinitely in prison where persons could not be brought to court and, if so, what is that law?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Such a law does not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So, do you agree with me that, even if the situation might have been an emergency situation, because of that situation the code of criminal procedure of Yugoslavia was anyway violated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my view, it would have been illegal to release persons who are suspected of having committed criminal acts, such acts for which the death penalty could be imposed, should they have been found guilty.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I see your point, but, in any case, even if this reasoning is acceptable, that means that, for emergency reasons, you were compelled to violate the code of criminal procedure of Yugoslavia, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that observing the principle of legality -- that is, the obligation of all State authorities to do everything within their power to prosecute persons suspected of such high crimes, that takes precedence over the rights to which you are alluding.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I can see even this point. By the way, is not Yugoslavia and the former Yugoslavia -- did the principle of compulsory penal action apply in the former Yugoslavia, or did the principle of discretionary penal action apply there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am afraid I do not understand this question. I do not know what you are implying by "discretionary" and "obligatory".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: It is a question of great importance. Maybe he can refer to the law of necessity where necessity creates its own law. I am not going into that -- it is a possible question on constitutional law.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I am getting to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: If his explanation is acceptable, would you not prefer turning to another question? He has given an explanation of why it was not possible to release those incarcerated at that time. I do not see what else he should say.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right. In any case, you did, in examination-in-chief, mention the code of criminal procedure of Yugoslavia as the laws which should rule these proceedings, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness nods head) Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Again, coming back to the 13 copies of records of statements of prisoners shown to you last Friday and where you recognised your signature, would you agree that these persons, prior to being questioned by your committee or your Commission, were not informed of any rights, were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What rights do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: The rights concerning the accused according to the Yugoslavian code of criminal procedure, the accused's rights to be warned about his rights -- is that not right -- did you advise these prisoners, before questioning them of any rights they might have according to regulations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All these individuals were invited to state the circumstances relating to the suspicion of their participation in armed rebellion, so they were advised before the questioning that there was reasonable grounds for suspicion that they committed such acts. Then, they were invited to state what they knew about it, that is, whether they had taken part in armed rebellion, and to state that freely before the Commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Yes, but this is not exactly what I wanted to say. What are the rights of the accused --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: What counsel is saying, before you questioned those accused persons or witnesses, whatever, did you read to them their entitlements as persons being questioned, as to what rights they had, whether they do not have to say anything, whether they have the right to counsel -- what did you spell out to them as to what rights they had before your Commission, or did they have no rights before your Commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, in any event, these persons were told that they could remain silent, that they could state what they had in their Defence, and, as far as the duty of the questioner is concerned, according to the law -- as far as the Defence counsel is concerned, for instance, the regulations governing the code of procedure was violated in that respect. However, since this was not an investigative procedure, this was a procedure based on an earlier charge -- in that respect, these persons could have been interrogated without the presence of their counsel and I said previously that the statements which were taken previously from these persons could not have been used in the court proceedings subsequently -- only the investigating judge could have advised the suspects that they had the rights to Defence counsel. However, since this is a pre-trial proceeding, this is an information interview, which could be a basis for, let us say, initiating some criminal proceedings, but, again, I repeat that it may not be used as a basis for reaching a final decision on that. So, again, I repeat: this statement had to be sealed in a separate envelope and kept separately. I believe that I was clear enough on that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: According to the court of criminal procedure in any case, this kind of interrogation was also dealt with with the same rights as the interrogation of an investigating judge; was that not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Objection, your Honours. The witness clarified that -- in this specific case, he mentioned that this is not the same procedure; this is the procedure which is not a court procedure. He said that this was an information interview and that sufficiently explains why the witnesses were not properly advised of the rights according to them, according to the procedure -- to the proper code of criminal procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Your Honour, since the witness, in examination-in-chief, mentioned precisely the code of criminal procedure in the former Yugoslavia, I think I am entitled to cross-examine him through this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You are -- actually, you are following it. I think what should be your next question --

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: My next question is, since he said that the prisoners were warned about their right to keep silent, why did you not give an account of this in the record, as it is provided by the code of criminal procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He has answered that question. He said it was not an investigation under the criminal procedure court. He was not acting as an investigating judge -- he was not even acting as a police officer. This is proceedings of a commission -- this is what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: But, your Honour, he said that he warned the prisoners of this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: That is fair enough but that does not mean the proceedings were under the code of criminal procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I asked why did he not give an account of that in the record about this warning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: And why was it no spelt out that the warnings had been given, or that no warning was necessary, or the type of warning they gave -- is that your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Yes, that is my question. Why was that not made clear in the record, that you actually did advise the prisoners of their right of keeping silent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember whether this was introduced into the records or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Since all this is not according to the code of criminal procedure and when you stated Friday that these persons were questioned according to the letter of the law, then please tell us exactly what law or regulations you were talking about in your examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I spoke on the law of criminal procedure for Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right, let us move on. Is it your testimony, Mr. Begtasovic, that proceedings were warranted against every single person interrogated by your Commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that, in my opinion, against most of these individuals, there were grounds for procedures of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And when did that happen; when were proceedings brought against the single persons interrogated by your Commission -- when the indictments took place, in how many cases?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Begtasovic, let us go back for a moment to the 13 statements taken by your Commission where you recognised your signature last Friday. Were these the only copies you have had occasion to see again in the last two years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And, by the way, I do not know whether you are in a position to answer this question, but do you know why only 13 of the over 100 interrogations that you conducted were brought here; do you have any idea -- are the other ones missing? Did you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have understood the question, but I do not know why we only have 13 brought to the Tribunal, as you yourself have just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right. You said in examination-in-chief, or in some cross-examination of co-defendants that you interviewed the prisoners in the SUP headquarters in Konjic; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, "SUP" is short for Secretariat of Internal Affairs. It is an organ of the police -- the executive organ -- and for some usual colloquial reasons we refer to it as the SUP building, but it is the building of the public security office in Konjic, in actual fact, so we are dealing with the same thing, SUP, MUP public security station, they are one and the same, dating back to Communistic terms -- SUP, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did those interviews always take place in the same room inside this building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure, but I think it was all done in the same room, and this was conditioned by the shelling, so that, as far as I am able to recall, the questioning took place on the first floor, because that was the safest place to have them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you meet every single prisoner only once, or more than once?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I met them only once.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did the prisoners -- were they brought to SUP from Musala in groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably two or three prisoners at a time -- two or three detainees at a time, so that two or three would wait in an antechamber, in a room in front of the room where the questioning took place, and then they would come in one by one and sit before the Commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I see. Were guards present in the room when the interrogations took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that the guards were not present in the room where the actual Commission was doing the questioning. They would wait in front of the door outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: You said that all five members of the Commission were present during the interview; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: How long did the single interviews take, approximately, more or less?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly, but I would suppose that we would hear daily seven or eight of these detainees.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Was there a typist present during the interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the typist?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember the face -- if you were to give me a name, I could say whether that was the name or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Was that Ismeta Pozder?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know her.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Were the five members, the typist and the detainee present or together the entire time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Also the recorder.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Were there the five members, the typist (the recorder) and the detainee all present the entire time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were present all the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This question has been answered on several occasions, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: You said that the record was typed during the interview itself as long as the prisoner gave his statement, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at the same time -- after the questioning. The questioned individual would sign the record and then members of the Commission and the recorder would do the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right. So you said that the previous statements of the previous commission were not used by you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Why did you not find it proper to give the prisoner the possibility to review his previous statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not find any justified reasons for this, or logical reasons, either.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Begtasovic, did you personally know any of the prisoners you happened to interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not know them personally, no. Perhaps I had seen some of the people around in Konjic, because Konjic is a small town -- I might have known them by sight, but I could not say exactly that I talked to them or was in any direct contact with any of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Let me mention a name to you. Does the name of Milenko Kuljanin say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it does not. "Kuljanin" is a fairly common surname. It is from the Bradina area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I mention Milenko Kuljanin, because he testified in this court that he was not really interviewed by your Commission but was simply requested to sign a record of statement, which had already been prepared -- is that possible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is absolutely not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: You would agree, Mr. Begtasovic, that, in interviewing persons, when the interviews are -- when two different interviews are separated by months -- I mean, two different interviews of the same person -- when the interviews are separated by months, do you agree that the interviewed person does not give the identical statement using identical language; in other words, even if the sense is the same, the exact same words will not be used -- is that not true? Was I clear in my question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was clear. I do not think the statement would be identical -- each on two occasions in the space of two days, let alone after several months have expired.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So, may I ask that the witness be shown Exhibits D16/4 and D15/4, which are two different statements of Milenko Kuljanin -- the one dated 8 June 1992 and the second one dated 11 January 1993. Would you please provide the witness with both statements -- D16/4 and D15/4. (Handed) Would you please, Mr. Begtasovic, compare these two statements and just take your time, of course, to compare them and just, for instance, could you please, just for an example, read out from the first statement -- I mean, first of all, I withdraw it. First of all, look at the statement of 11 January and tell me do you recognise your signature on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So, let us start from this record of statement -- the one dated 11 January 1993. Would you please read out the 10 lines from the third paragraph -- the one which starts with the words "I was at home when the attack on Bradina started" -- do you see this on 11 January 1993 statement. Could you please read it out, just 10 lines of this statement -- read it out aloud, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "I was at home when the attack on Bradina started. I took my rifle and with my unit -- "

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Begtasovic, start again and very slowly, please, would you read it very slowly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes: "I was at home when the attack on Bradina started. I took my rifle and went to the positions, to Bratisava with my unit. I spent about 24 hours at the position, then retreated towards Jasika. The following men from Brdani remained at Bratisava: Draganic Marko, Draganic Jovo, Draganic Milan, Sinikovic Velo, Sinikovic Goran, Sinikovic Slobodan, Sinikovic Gojko, Sinikovic Vojo, and Sinikovic Branko who intended to break through to the village of Brdani. I met Mrkajic Momir, Gligorevic Brano and Gligorevic Milovan in Jasika and we decided to try and make it to Hadzici across Mount Bjelasnica."

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: That is okay. Could you take the other statement, the one dated 8 June 1992, and go to the third paragraph starting with the same words, "I was at home when the attack on Bradina started" -- would you please read these 10 lines, also?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes: "I was at home at the time of the attack on Bradina. Then I took my rifle and proceeded to the positions at Bratisava with my unit. I spent about 24 hours at the position, then retreated towards Jasika. The following men from Brdani remained at Bratisava: Draganic Marko, Draganic Jovo, Draganic Milan, Sinikovic Velo, Sinikovic Goran, Sinikovic Slobodan, Sinikovic Gojko, Sinikovic Vojo and Sinikovic Branko who intended to break through to the village of Brdani. I met Momir Mrkajic, Brano Gligorevic and Milovan Gligorevic in Jasika and we decided to try and make it to Hadzici across Mount Bjelasnica."

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that these two passages you read out are absolutely identical, word by word, in the two documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Do you have any explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no other explanation apart from saying that, when I attended the questioning -- when I questioned this individual, if it was myself who questioned him, that I had in my hands this statement of the previous commission, and that I used it in the questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is not what you said so far about the procedure of questioning the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said previously that I only took a brief view of the statements that existed in the files. I did not have this in mind, but now, when I come to compare these two texts, the only explanation is the one that I have just given you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have more accurate translations now of these two statements such as to show in both characters the parts which are identical in the two statements. We have copies for your Honours and for the Defence lawyers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I thought he explained why it so happened -- why he had -- why now you can compare? (Handed)

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Begtasovic, I would like you to be provided with annex D45 from the Vejzagic second binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Is it true of all the Defence statements produced the day before last -- they have common passages to the statements which they made in the Celebici camp?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: The Defence statements produced the day before -- do you mean last Friday?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: There common passages with the statements made by these detainees in the Celebici camp?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: If you are talking about the 13 statements, we do not know, because we do not have the statements of both commissions for every one of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I see. (Document handed)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Do we still wait for you?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Sorry, just to answer your Honour's question, there are exhibits D42/1, and D43/1 concerning Novica Dzordzic, which are also identical passages -- D42/1 and D43/1, Novica Dzordzic. Do you recognise Dzumhur's signature on this statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Which document is the witness being shown -- could you identify the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: V-D45 from the second binder of Mr. Vejzagic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will now rise. We will reassemble at 4.30 so you can streamline your presentation. (4.00pm) (A short break) (4.30pm) (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Please remind the witness he is still on his oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I remind you, Sir, that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may proceed now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I will withdraw my previous question and I will go to another issue. Mr. Begtasovic, are you aware that the previous commission resigned before completing its work because of the mistreatment of the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not know that the previous commission resigned at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: May I ask that the witness be provided with Prosecution Exhibit 162, please? (Handed) Did you ever see this document, Mr. Begtasovic? Do you know it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I have never seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: You see that this document is addressed to three authorities -- one of them being the "coordinator" or "combat coordinator". Do you know who the "coordinator" is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The witness answered, but even before replying to this question, he had already stated that he had never seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Do you know who had control and command over the prisons of Musala and Celebici during 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: By the way, in your position of a prominent citizen and civil servant of Konjic, and during your work in the Investigating Commission, did you get to know anything about a man by the name "Belalic", initial "B", "Bosnia", as responsible for detainees in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I have not heard that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: May I ask that the witness be provided with Prosecution Exhibit 214, please? You see this document is dated 22 December 1992? Do you agree that it was 15 days before your appointment as a member of the Commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to the date indicated, that is how it appears.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you ever see this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I have never seen that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Would you agree -- that is a general question -- do you agree that telexes, since they go through a machine, do not have signatures and seals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question? I did not understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Would you agree that telexes, since they go through a machine, do not have signatures or seals on them -- would you agree on that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since I am completely ignorant in things technical, including transmission of documents, I really cannot answer you. I am not sure whether this can be transmitted or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Let me read out the five lines starting with, "From the first days of the war" from this document and ask you something: "From the first days of the war -- "

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, objection -- the witness does not recognise this document, so I do not understand what purpose his reading of it serves.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Just forget about the document, Mr. Begtasovic. I want to ask you whether a given statement I am going to tell you is true or not. So, the statement is this one: "From the first days of the war, in the area of our municipality, 455 persons of the aggressor were registered as captured. The same were placed in the Celebici barracks and the sports hall in Konjic and, at the same time, a Military Investigation Commission was formed, composed of the representatives of the TO and HVO from Konjic -- people with adequate knowledge to conduct these affairs." Is this a true statement, as far as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: How can he give this opinion?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Does this statement -- is this statement consistent with your personal knowledge of what happened in the area in 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Personal knowledge derived from what -- what source?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: From his knowledge about what happened in the area of Konjic in 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He was a judge. How would he knows about these things -- if it is something that has come to his knowledge as an officer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You might be able to put questions to him about what happened about that time, and if he knows it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Generally, yes, but how can you ask him specific questions like this?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Begtasovic, is that true, that after people were captured and placed in Celebici barracks, and the sports hall in Konjic, at that time, a Military Investigation Commission was formed composed of the representatives of the TO and HVO from Konjic -- people with adequate knowledge to conduct these affairs -- is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The witness already answered this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: If he knows about it, he should be able to answer. He was there, he was an official, if these are things which he could know about, he would be able to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Would you answer my question -- is that a true statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard your question and I will give you an answer. During the work of the Commission of which I was a member, I was aware of the fact that, before the Commission of which I was a member, a different commission had been formed, which interrogated people who were detained at Celebici. As to the composition of this commission, including representatives of the TO and the HVO, that, I do not know -- I do not recall that any more. I doubt whether I had such precise information, even at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And is that a true statement, that: "Towards the end of December 1992, in Konjic, the investigation for the war prisoners had not been completed and it was requested to the Ministry of Defence to intervene urgently with the relevant State institutions so that a decree with powers of law be passed concerning abolition, that is amnesty of certain categories of individuals, perpetrators of criminal acts." Was that true and was that the reason for which your Commission was appointed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not aware of this. I did not have that knowledge then; I do not possess such knowledge now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I am coming to the end of my cross-examination. You reported that none of the persons you interrogated complained to you that they had been mistreated while in Celebici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you ask any of the persons you interrogated whether they had been mistreated while in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure of that. It is possible that I did ask them, but I do not remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: You discussed the Bosnian citizenship laws and the fact that they changed at various times. Can you tell us the difference between the law in April 1992, the law in the fall of 1992, and the law of 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as the crucial differences are concerned, there are no such differences in these two laws. The provisions regarding application for citizenship are identical -- as far as the basic provisions for cessation of it are concerned are also the same. However, maybe we should point out that there is a provision in this current law pursuant to which all citizens of the former SFRY, citizens who lived in the territory of BH on 6 April 1992, still have their citizenship.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: You say that there were not crucial differences. What were then the non-crucial differences?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is this last provision that I mentioned in this last answer to you and right now I cannot recall any other.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: You discussed the procedure for renouncing citizenship, but did I understand you correctly that the relevant bodies, including the court, were not functioning after April 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that, after April 1992, the basic court in Konjic was not functioning and there were no other regular courts that were able to function or that did function in the Konjic area and that includes both the courts and the Prosecutor's Office.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Begtasovic, is that correct, that you in 1993, you interviewed Mr. Delic and Mr. Landzo and, further, that you have already --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: This is a matter that I sent a letter to the Prosecution earlier about discussing. It is a matter we object to relevance, it is a matter that has been brought before this court before and it is a matter that I believe this witness has a privilege to invoke. I am going to let him speak on that. Also, under Rule 89(D), it is a matter that should be excluded from consideration by this court. This court has ruled before that documents by the Prosecution had been admitted for the limited purpose of identity of names only, but this matter is totally irrelevant to this proceeding before this court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We have not heard the question yet. You anticipate --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, we anticipated it for several days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We should know the question before ruling on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: May I finish my question. May I also say that the reason for questioning that -- my question is: is that correct, is it not, that you in 1993, interviewed Mr. Delic and Mr. Landzo and, further, is that true that you have already given a witness statement yourself concerning those interviews in front of another judge of Konjic? I am asking this question, because it is related to the position of Mr. Delalic in Konjic at the time, and this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Delic or Delalic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Delalic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Delalic was not in Konjic I thought in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: This is a question, the reason for which will become clear in the following part, if I am allowed to ask it. Was that true, Mr. Begtasovic, that you interviewed Mr. Delic and Mr. Landzo in 1993, and that, after that, you gave a witness statement yourself concerning those interviews to Judge Sena Uzunovic in 1994.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As to the first part of your question, my answer is yes, in the affirmative. I did question -- and I cannot claim whether this was in 1993 -- it is possible, but I am not sure of the date -- I questioned Mr. Landzo and Mr. Delic and, as far as the second part of your question is concerned, I do not recall that I was called up as a witness in a case and that I was questioned as a witness, especially not before Judge Senad Uzunovic, because there is no judge with such first and last names.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Sena Uzunovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sena Uzunovic does exist, it is a female judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Is that the case, that on 6 April 1994, Judge Sena Uzunovic took a witness statement from you about your interviews of Mr. Landzo and Mr. Delic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you were to show me a record of it, I could answer you in the affirmative or the negative, but I do not remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: May I ask the usher to show to the witness this document, which is already in the possession of the Prosecution -- I ask it be marked for identification. These are copies --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: What is the statement about?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: This is a draft of the statement he was telling me that, if he sees it, he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Yes, but what is the statement about? There will be a question of whether or not the statement is relevant here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: It is a witness statement given by Mr. Begtasovic to investigating Judge Sena Uzunovic in Konjic about his interviews of Mr. Landzo and Mr. Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: We object to the relevance --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do not have the document that he is referring to, either. We do not have that. We do not know what he is showing to the witness at the moment and, if he wants to pursue this line of questioning, I would ask the leave of the court to take the witness on voir dire about this issue, also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I do not see the relevance of this at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: In those statements in front of Mr. Begtasovic, Mr. Landzo and Mr. Delic were asked to make statements about the position in Celebici --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I am going to object --

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: In 1992 and his superiors -- Landzo and Delic were asked statements about their position in Celebici --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: We have reason to believe that this happened in their statement, about the positions of themselves and their superiors. This is why we believe that this is relevant. We are not interested in bringing in this statement, this witness statement of Mr. Begtasovic for any other reason -- not for any other part of its contents.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Counsel's microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Whose statement are we dealing with now?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: The statement -- I hope your Honours received copies of this statement of Mr. Begtasovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is his own statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: His own witness statement in front of Judge Sena Uzunovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: A statement producing somebody else's statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: This is a witness statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: A statement of a co-accused --

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Given by Mr. Begtasovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He is repeating a statement of a co-accused against another co-accused -- is that what your position is?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we object, because this is a statement against a co-accused and I think this is against the Rules. This cannot be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I also believe that this is privileged information according to the continental form of law in Yugoslavia, that this is part of a proceedings where an investigating judge is reporting to another investigating judge, which is privileged information and they have a duty not to disclose that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Also, your Honour, I would object, besides those grounds, under Rule 66(B).

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Also under Rule 89(D), your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: We have to emphasise that, with respect to Rule 66, we made the entire file available to the Defence lawyers many, many, many months ago. I would like to state that I am not asking this question for the specifics of the crime Mr. Begtasovic was investigating at the time when he interviewed Mr. Landzo and Mr. Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: That is what I was asking -- a statement -- he is presenting a statement of a co-accused against another co-accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: The same of the statements which were admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: What statement has been admitted -- a statement of a co-accused against another co-accused, how can it be used?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: These statements are not -- were not disclosed in the evidence which we received and, also, it is a procedure that is privileged information according to our legislation and I want to advise the witness that he is in violation of our own Rules of Procedure if he discloses such material.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Our position is that this is admissible against Delic and Landzo and your Honours can later consider whether to admit it with respect to Mr. Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I am confused. I do not know how this man's statement given to somebody else can be admissible against my client. Unless he is talking about the statements that were previously introduced by the Prosecutor for the sole purpose of the names and titles of people in there, and in that case, there is no substantive facts that are introduced against my client, and -- I am just befuddled.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the further objection under Rule 66 is I have never seen this document before, as I am sure none of the other counsel for defendants on this side have ever seen this document before. At least before we go further with this, we would like to have one moment to sit down and at least ascertain what this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: As far as the discovery issue is concerned, all the Defence lawyers had an opportunity to see all the Bubalo file -- I was not yet in the trial team at that time. If your Honours wish, Ms. McHenry can explain how that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I am still at a loss how the Bubalo matter is in any way relevant to any of the accusations in the indictment in this case -- two accused, or maybe all of the defendants, of just being bad people in general, and they are not on trial for being bad people in general -- they are on trial for specific allegations.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Actually, we are not wishing to introduce the Bubalo affair in this trial. This question can deal with information about the position of Mr. Delalic in Konjic and with respect to Celebici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I have read it myself and I really do not see any connection between the accused persons and the present trial we have here. If anything might have happened in some other proceedings elsewhere, I think that is a quite different position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Where does the statement show that Delalic was the superior of Delic and Landzo in respect of the Celebici camp? Where does it show that? Read that portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: There might be a possibility to clarify that question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Why bring in unnecessary matters that do not relate to our case? In any case a statement of a co-accused against another co-accused --

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: This document is only intended to refresh his memory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: About what?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: He said, "I do not see the record, I do not remember." This is why we wanted to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: To that extent, maybe you can show it to him for that, but nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Speaking for myself, I do not think it is admissible for this purpose. If there is another way of bringing it in, I do not know, but definitely not through this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We have already seen some documents which indicate that Delalic had probably directed Delic to commit the murder of Bubalo. We do not know whether Bubalo was a person detained in the camp -- and that charge was later on dropped.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Could we ask the witness what Mr. Delic and Mr. Landzo said about their own position in Celebici --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honours!

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honours!

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours!

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Where is it in the statement you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Some of this sounds fairly strange. I think there are circumstances when perhaps one could introduce a witness linking accused persons, but not in these circumstances. I do not see how you could. I seized the opportunity to read through this statement and I am not satisfied that there is a sufficient linkage.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right, your Honour. So, my cross-examination is finished. Thank you, Mr. Begtasovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Is there any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would first of all like to ask that this document, which has been identified, be taken out of the evidence material, away from the evidence material of this court. I have just one question for the witness and you thought that the document was irrelevant for the witness as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Begtasovic, in the course of your examination and re-examination, you said that you questioned most of the 105 individuals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I questioned most of those 105 witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you recall the exact names of the individuals that you did not question yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor showed you a statement by somebody named Milenko Kuljanin and you said you did not know him. Do you recall if you personally questioned that particular individual?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall whether I questioned him personally. It is possible that I did, but there is also the possibility that another member of the Commission questioned him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think this is all we have for this witness. Thank you very much for your effort and for assisting the Trial Chamber. I think you are discharged.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Can we have your next witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we should first of all like to know whether we are going to continue the cross-examination of the Brigadier?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: On Thursday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The Prosecutor actually made a special application for that and not only him -- all the other counsel requested for time within which to conduct the cross-examination. I thought, because of the amount of material you assembled, it might not be unreasonable to allow cross-examination on Thursday, leaving two clear days within which to work through it. So I think we will still wait until Thursday to determine the cross-examination -- it is possible a lot of cross-examination may not materialise, depending on what the Prosecutor discovers, but let him have ample time to work through the amount of material you have already presented.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
